Ghanaguru
of Hārīta family, father of Śrīnivāsadāsa (a. of Paratattvaprakāśikā. vaiṣ.

Ghanaguruvarya
son of Varadaguru of Kauśikagotra.
--Kandarpavijaya. bhāṇa.

Ghanarāgakīrtanādi
music compositions in some of the major Rāgas by Rāmavarma Svāti Tirunāl Mahārāja. Tra. Ad.

Ghanarāma
son of Govardhana.
--Śrāddhapradīpa. Baroda 9971. PUL. I. p. 104. [Page273-b]

Ghanavṛtta
kāvya; a continuation of Kālidāsa's Meghadūta. by Korāḍa Rāmacandra, a modern writer.
Pt.. Masulipatam, 1908.

Ghanavyūhasūtra
Bud. Skt. mostly in verse. AMG. II. p. 239. AR. XX. p. 433. Kanjur Kyoto 778. Nanjio 444. 782. 971. (Chin. transl. 618-907 A. D.).
Q. in Maitreyanātha's Bhavasaṅkrāntiṭīkā, Adyar edn. p. 45; the verse q. here is not to be found in the Tibetan transl. of it in Kanjur.

Ghanaśyāma
grandfather of Kāśīśvara Śarmā (a. of Jñānāmṛta, gr.). See NCC. IV. p. 142a.

Ghanaśyāma
scholar who conferred the title Anuṣṭupcakravartin on Bhāvabhaṭṭa, a. of Anūpasaṅgītavilāsa (See ch. I. verses 39-44).

Ghanaśyāma
alias Cauṇḍāji Panth; versatile an. arrogant writer from Mahārāṣṭra who lived in Tanjore a. a minister of king Tukkojī I (1729-35 A. D.); also called Āryaka (See

); an. had the titles Sarvajñakavi, Vaśyavacas, Kaṇṭhīrava an. Sarasvatī; born in January 1706 (on his horoscope see JOR. Madras IV. p.. 71-77); son of Kāśī an. Mahādeva (father's name is not Kāśīmahādeva a. given on the basis of col. Kāśīmahā- [Page274-a. devasūnu,
; see Intro. to C. on Campūrāmāyaṇa,

yasyezo 'grabhavaH pitA kila mahAdevaH sa kAzIprasaH; delete the entry Kāśīmahādeva from NCC. IV. p. 135b); grandson of Cauṇḍabālāji of Mauna Bhārgava family (his mother's father being Timmāji Bālāji of Kauṇḍinyagotra); younger brother of Īśa (who became a. ascetic assuming the name Cidambara Brahman who settled in Devīpaṭṭana near Navapāṣāṇa); had two wives Sundarī an. Kamalā (joint a.s of C. on Viddhasālabhañjikā,

), an. a sister Śākambharī; father of Candraśekhara (a. of C. on Ghanaśyāma's Ḍamaruka an. Pracaṇḍarāhūdaya) an. Govardhana (blind from birth an. a. of C. on Ghaṭakarpara, see above); in C. on Nīlakaṇṭhavijaya he says he composed 64 works in Skt., 20 in Pkt. an. 25 in vernaculars; his wives give a long list of his works in the beg. of their C. on Viddhasālabhañjikā,
